network.overall_strategy: Use the cyanosulfidic construction of the proline aminonitrile as the experimentally best-supported backbone, followed by explicitly unquantified nitrile hydration and amide hydrolysis. L-proline is represented separately from its D-enantiomer: successful achiral synthesis produces approximately equal amounts, not isolated or enantioenriched L-proline. The ten graph-distinct pathways comprise nine combinations of three HCN supply options and three acetylene supply options, plus one copper-assisted photoreduction variant. They are feedstock-supply and processing alternatives, not ten independently demonstrated proline-skeleton syntheses; the supplied literature does not support the latter claim. Methane-discharge supply channels are lumped source reactions, with their limitations identified individually. All numerical operating ranges below are proposed experimental screening windows, not reconstructed published procedures; 254 nm irradiation and the reported 32% yield over two late precursor-forming operations are the principal quantitative observations taken from the supplied account of Patel et al. (2015). That yield is neither an isolated yield for every encoded step nor an end-to-end proline yield. Sulfide-poor copper-mediated hydrocyanation is separated from sulfide-rich photochemistry because copper sulfide precipitation can deactivate the catalyst. Reactive aldehyde and imine intermediates are trapped locally rather than transported. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis requires an independently tested compatibility and residence-time window. Neutral reference formulas represent pH-dependent solution species; S8 is a formal sulfur redox endpoint, not an assertion that the actual photochemical sulfur products were established. The restricted role vocabulary requires terminal coproducts to be labeled intermediate. Elemental balancing must not be used to infer enantiomeric ratios. No oxygen, enzymes, modern hydride reagents, or unsupported enantioselective purification step is assumed.

molecules.common_name: Hydrogen sulfide; reference form of dissolved H2S/HS-
Elemental sulfur; formal terminal redox reservoir
Proline aminonitrile; achirally generated racemic pool

reactions.name: Copper(I)-mediated hydrocyanation of acetylene

conditions.pressure: Approximately 1 bar total; screen acetylene partial pressures of 0.001-0.1 bar
conditions.catalyst: Cu(I)-cyanide species; proposed total copper screen of 10-100 micromolar
conditions.other: Anoxic, sulfide-poor source pool; screen pH 7.5-9.0 and total cyanide 1-10 mM over 4-48 h. Measure dissolved acetylene and copper rather than assuming gas-liquid equilibration or complete catalyst dissolution. Keep sulfide delivery downstream. A localized copper-bearing deposit or evaporite is required; crust-wide copper abundance is not assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Copper-mediated activation of acetylene permits addition of HCN across its triple bond, producing acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This entry reaction is explicitly identified in the cyanosulfidic framework (Patel et al., 2015, DOI: 10.1038/nchem.2202). The supplied report does not establish the exact catalyst speciation, loading, pH, or operating rate; the listed values are screening proposals. Sulfide can precipitate copper, so simultaneous unrestricted copper and sulfide availability is not assumed. Physical separation of the copper-bearing source region from the subsequent sulfidic pool is chemically motivated, but acrylonitrile recovery and dissolved-copper carryover must be measured.

reactions.name: Aza-Michael addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Screen pH 8.5-9.5, acrylonitrile 0.1-5 mM, and total ammonia/ammonium 10-100 mM over 6-168 h. Ammonia excess is intended to limit repeated Michael addition. Such concentrations require local concentration, not an unconcentrated ocean. Measure oligomers and multiply alkylated amines. Cyanamide is not included in the selected feed.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia attacks the beta carbon of the activated alkene, followed by proton transfer to give 3-aminopropanenitrile.
reactions.reasoning: The supplied account identifies this transformation on the proline branch (Patel et al., 2015). No mineral catalyst is required by the reaction chemistry. High ammonia availability, competing addition products, and reagent staging remain experimental constraints. Cyanamide could divert the free amino functionality toward guanidinylated products; its absence here is a feed-composition assumption, not a claim that such competing chemistry disappears naturally.

reactions.name: Sulfide-driven photoreductive conversion of the C3 nitrile to an aldehyde

conditions.other: Anoxic thin water layer; screen pH 7.5-9.0, substrate 0.1-5 mM, and total dissolved sulfide 1-20 mM. Use 254 nm irradiation as the reported laboratory reference; proposed photon-flux screen 1e13-1e15 photons cm^-2 s^-1 for 1-48 h. Follow with broadband anoxic surface-UV tests rather than assuming 254 nm performance transfers to sunlight. Quantify sulfide remaining after Fe2+-driven precipitation. Trap the aldehyde locally in rxn_004.

reactions.mechanism: Photogenerated reducing equivalents reduce the nitrile to an imine-level intermediate; hydrolysis gives 3-aminopropanal and ammonia. Oxidation of sulfide supplies the reducing equivalents.
reactions.reasoning: Reductive nitrile homologation and the C3 amino-nitrile branch are supported by the supplied account of Patel et al. (2015). The framework permits sulfide photochemistry without added copper, but the supplied excerpts do not establish the substrate-specific rate under this exact catalyst-free window. Ranjan et al. (2018) identify dissolved sulfidic-anion availability as a substantive geochemical constraint. S8 provides a balanceable formal oxidation endpoint; actual polysulfide and other sulfur products must be characterized. No isolated aldehyde yield or transport lifetime is asserted.

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin homologation of 3-aminopropanal

conditions.other: Screen pH 7.5-8.5 and total cyanide 1-10 mM. Introduce the cyanide-bearing stream at the aldehyde-generation zone; test trapping over minutes to 6 h. Do not store or transfer a concentrated free-aldehyde pool. Measure competing carbonyl reactions and cyanide volatilization.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide adds to the aldehyde carbonyl, and protonation produces 4-amino-2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This is the cyanohydrin-forming homologation described for the amino-nitrile branch (Patel et al., 2015). Local trapping addresses aldehyde instability more plausibly than a long cross-environment transfer. The achievable flux depends on cyanide concentration, competing ammonia chemistry, and aldehyde losses; none is quantified by the supplied report. Formation of a stereogenic center under these achiral conditions does not establish an L-bias.

reactions.name: Sulfurization and five-membered cyclic hydroxythioamide formation

conditions.other: Screen pH 8.0-9.0, cyanohydrin 0.1-5 mM, and dissolved sulfide 1-20 mM over 12-168 h. Initially examine dark incubations to distinguish sulfurization from subsequent photochemistry. Determine the cyclic-to-open-chain hydroxythioamide ratio and dependence on residual ammonia.

reactions.mechanism: Nitrile sulfurization establishes thioamide functionality; intramolecular substitution by the terminal amino group forms a five-membered thiolactam with ammonia loss. This node lumps sulfurization and ring closure rather than asserting an isolated elementary mechanism.
reactions.reasoning: The supplied account reports cyclic and open-chain alpha-hydroxythioamides in this branch (Patel et al., 2015). Only the productive cyclic branch is represented; the open-chain material is not falsely counted as a demonstrated additional proline pathway. The chronological order and individual rate constants of sulfur incorporation and cyclization are not established by the provided excerpts. High residual ammonia and sulfide scavenging by abundant Fe2+ could affect throughput.

reactions.name: Photodeoxygenation of the cyclic hydroxythioamide

conditions.other: Screen pH 7.5-9.0, cyclic hydroxythioamide 0.1-2 mM, and dissolved sulfide 1-20 mM. Reference irradiation: 254 nm; proposed flux 1e13-1e15 photons cm^-2 s^-1 and exposure 1-48 h. Follow thiolactam formation and photodestruction separately. Avoid carrying copper-containing solids into this sulfidic stage.

reactions.mechanism: Photoreductive cleavage of the alpha C-O bond replaces the hydroxyl functionality with hydrogen, yielding gamma-butyrothiolactam.
reactions.reasoning: Gamma-butyrothiolactam is reported as the deoxygenated thioamide product of this branch (Patel et al., 2015). That observation supports the chosen ring-forming route, but not a yield or rate at the proposed environmental settings. Sulfide is a consumable reductant rather than a mineral catalyst. The S8 output is formal redox bookkeeping; it does not imply an elementary reaction involving eight substrate molecules.

reactions.name: Photoreductive thiolactam conversion to a transient cyclic imine

conditions.other: Screen pH 7.5-9.0, thiolactam 0.1-2 mM, and dissolved sulfide 1-10 mM under 254 nm irradiation. Use a proposed flux range of 1e13-1e15 photons cm^-2 s^-1 and sample over 1-24 h. Cyanide for rxn_008 is present in the same reaction zone so the imine need not accumulate. Stop irradiation based on measured aminonitrile formation, not an assumed fixed residence time.

reactions.mechanism: Reduction and sulfur loss from the thiolactam are proposed to generate 1-pyrroline, immediately trapped in rxn_008. H2S appears on both sides because donor sulfide oxidation and release of thiolactam-bound sulfur as sulfide can occur in the gross bookkeeping; the net sulfur endpoint is represented formally as S8.
reactions.reasoning: The thiolactam-to-aminonitrile transformation is supported by Patel et al. (2015), whereas the discrete 1-pyrroline intermediate is inferred in the supplied report. This node and rxn_008 factor a coupled transformation; they are not claims that pyrroline was isolated or that sulfur speciation was measured. The reported 32% over two late precursor-forming operations must not be assigned to this node alone. Competing overreduction or photodestruction must be assayed; rapid cyanide capture is a proposed selectivity safeguard, not demonstrated geological throughput.

reactions.name: Cyanide capture of the cyclic imine to form proline aminonitrile

conditions.other: Same reaction zone as rxn_007; screen pH 7.5-9.0 and total cyanide 1-10 mM. No isolated-imine storage or environmental transfer. Measure aminonitrile formation, pyrrolidine from overreduction, and remaining thiolactam. Achiral reagents imply approximately equal configurations at the newly formed stereocenter.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide adds to the electrophilic carbon of the cyclic imine or iminium species, followed by proton transfer to give pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Proline aminonitrile is the reported endpoint of the resolved precursor sequence (Patel et al., 2015). Ritson (2021) identifies unusual retention of the proline aminonitrile under conditions that favor reversion of other aminonitriles. This supports its selection as an accumulation and transfer intermediate, but does not provide a quantitative lifetime in the proposed mixed solution. Neither the cited aminonitrile yield nor its relative persistence demonstrates subsequent hydrolysis to free proline.

reactions.name: Acid-catalyzed hydration of proline aminonitrile to prolinamide

conditions.other: Screen aminonitrile 0.1-10 mM and reaction times from 1 to 90 days. A candidate setting is an anoxic HCl-bearing volcanic condensate pool downstream of the photochemical pool. Test the actual crude photochemical mixture as well as purified analytical controls. Transfer is limited to the comparatively persistent aminonitrile, with proposed transport times of hours rather than storage of aldehyde or imine. Sulfide outgassing, cyanide loss, and recovery during acidification must be quantified.

reactions.mechanism: Protonation activates the nitrile for water addition; subsequent proton transfers and tautomerization form the carboxamide.
reactions.reasoning: Chemically conventional but unquantified for the reported proline precursor mixture. Patel et al. (2015), as summarized in the supplied research, does not establish a yield for aminonitrile hydrolysis to proline. Ritson (2021) supports relative aminonitrile retention, not successful hydration under this proposed acidic window. This is an explicit enabling bottleneck: the numerical conditions are tests, not evidence that a natural acidic pool supplies adequate rate, selectivity, or residence time. No concentration-preserving transfer or cleanup efficiency is assumed.

reactions.name: Prolinamide hydrolysis to an equimolar L-proline and D-proline pool

conditions.other: Continue in the hydrolysis pool without requiring prolinamide isolation. Screen 1-180 days while maintaining acidity against released ammonia. Independently constrain mol_016:mol_017 to approximately 1:1 for an achiral starting pool; elemental balancing alone cannot determine this ratio. Quantify free proline separately from hydrolyzable precursors using secondary-amine-compatible and enantiomer-resolving analytics. OPA-only assays are unsuitable.

reactions.mechanism: Acid-catalyzed amide hydrolysis replaces the amide nitrogen with hydroxyl functionality, releasing ammonia and retaining the pyrrolidine skeleton. Both proline enantiomers result from the racemic precursor pool.
reactions.reasoning: Ordinary amide chemistry makes this endpoint plausible, but the supplied account of Patel et al. (2015) provides no prolinamide-to-proline yield or validated natural residence time. The full finishing sequence therefore remains unquantified. Parker et al. (2011) documents the analytical blind spot of OPA/NAC for proline. No extrapolated hydrothermal half-life is used to guarantee recovery. Klussmann et al. (2006) demonstrated conditional phase-based enantiomeric amplification, but that result does not justify spontaneous production of pure L-proline here; no chloroform cosolvate or unprovided chiral seed is introduced.

reactions.name: Methane-ammonia discharge channel supplying hydrogen cyanide

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K cooled bulk gas and collection water; nonthermal discharge energy is additional
conditions.other: Anoxic local reducing gas pocket; screen CH4:NH3 molar ratios of 1:1-10:1 and intermittent discharge for 1-24 h. Discharge electron energies are not represented by the bulk temperature. Collect HCN into nearby water, provisionally at pH 9-10 to reduce volatilization, then determine recovery into rxn_001. No globally methane-ammonia-dominated atmosphere or known natural collection efficiency is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Lumped radical chemistry converts carbon and nitrogen from methane and ammonia into HCN, with hydrogen as a formal coproduct. This is a net productive channel, not the complete discharge-product inventory.
reactions.reasoning: HCN generation and subsequent amino-acid precursor chemistry are established features of reducing discharge experiments (Miller, 1957; Ring et al., 1972). Those studies do not establish the proposed source concentration or coupling efficiency to the cyanosulfidic sequence. Proline detection in discharge mixtures is not treated as proof that this particular downstream mechanism operated. The exact net channel and proposed collection schedule require quantitative validation.

reactions.name: Methane-nitrogen discharge channel supplying hydrogen cyanide

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K cooled bulk gas and collection water; energetic discharge zones are nonthermal
conditions.other: Screen CH4:N2 molar ratios of 0.01-0.3 in an anoxic gas mixture and discharge exposure of 1-24 h. Determine HCN production per delivered energy and its collection into water. Additional ammonia remains an external cofeed for rxn_002. This source is viable only in sufficiently reducing local gas compositions.

reactions.mechanism: Energetic activation of nitrogen and methane generates reactive nitrogen and carbon fragments whose recombination can form HCN; hydrogen is a formal coproduct.
reactions.reasoning: This is a candidate HCN-supply channel, not a demonstrated independent proline synthesis. Nitrogen-containing reducing discharge systems provide the relevant precedent (Ring et al., 1972), but the supplied report does not verify this isolated CH4/N2 channel at the stated composition or energy input. Its geological productivity is therefore speculative. Explicit N2 activation avoids implying that methane and nitrogen react at the stated bulk temperature without an external energy source.

reactions.name: Methane discharge channel supplying acetylene

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K cooled bulk gas; dissociation occurs in energetic discharge zones
conditions.other: Anoxic methane-bearing gas with repeated discharge and rapid cooling; screen total exposure of 1-24 h. Directly assay acetylene, other C2 hydrocarbons, soot, and hydrogen. Feed the recovered acetylene-bearing gas into the sulfide-poor rxn_001 pool without assuming selective acetylene isolation or a large atmospheric acetylene partial pressure.

reactions.mechanism: Lumped methane dissociation, carbon-carbon radical recombination, and further dehydrogenation generate an acetylene-containing gas mixture.
reactions.reasoning: Methane-discharge carbon coupling provides a chemically recognizable alternative to carbide-derived acetylene. However, the supplied research does not establish an acetylene yield sufficient for this network, so its geological supply role is speculative. Hydrocarbon-discharge amino-acid studies are contextual precedent, not direct validation of this source channel or its coupling to proline synthesis (Ring and Miller, 1984). No thermal conversion of methane at 300 K is implied.

reactions.name: Calcium carbide hydrolysis supplying acetylene

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K after water dilution and heat dissipation
conditions.other: Water encounters a surviving carbide-bearing impact deposit. Acetylene evolves promptly; calcium hydroxide makes the local solution strongly alkaline, potentially pH 11-12.5. Transfer the evolved gas, rather than the alkaline mineral slurry, into the separate rxn_001 pool. Verify temperature excursions, carbide inventory, gas losses, and absence of blocking surface layers.

reactions.mechanism: Water protonates acetylide carbon, releasing acetylene and producing calcium hydroxide.
reactions.reasoning: The inorganic hydrolysis is well established, and impact-derived metal-carbide hydrolysis is the proposed acetylene source in the cyanosulfidic scenario (Patel et al., 2015). Selecting calcium carbide makes the substrate and coproduct explicit; it does not establish that a sufficient natural CaC2 inventory existed. Carbide formation is outside this network and remains a feedstock assumption. Gas transfer is chemically justified because the hydroxide-rich slurry would otherwise disrupt the downstream pH window.

reactions.name: Copper-assisted alternative for photoreductive C3 nitrile conversion

conditions.catalyst: Cu(I)/Cu(II)-cyanide species; proposed total copper 1-10 micromolar
conditions.other: Screen pH 8.0-9.0, substrate 0.1-5 mM, dissolved sulfide 1-10 mM, and total cyanide 1-10 mM under 254 nm irradiation at 1e13-1e15 photons cm^-2 s^-1 for 1-48 h. Cyanide also supports downstream trapping in rxn_004. Measure dissolved copper, Cu sulfide precipitation, and photochemical rate against matched copper-free controls. Retain this variant only if an active soluble or otherwise characterized copper fraction persists.

reactions.mechanism: Copper photoredox cycling can mediate reducing-equivalent transfer from sulfide to the nitrile; hydrolysis of the reduced nitrogen functionality then releases the aldehyde and ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reports that copper cycling can accelerate the broader cyanosulfidic photochemistry. The supplied excerpts do not validate this exact substrate, copper loading, or sulfide/cyanide mixture. This is consequently a conditional process variant rather than another proven proline route. Copper precipitation and sulfidic-anion supply are explicit rejection criteria, not assumed solved constraints (Ranjan et al., 2018). Its purpose is to test a genuine catalyst-availability alternative without introducing an unsupported carbon-skeleton transformation.

pathways.name: Externally supplied HCN and acetylene; copper-free sulfidic photochemistry
pathways.description: Reference backbone with HCN, acetylene, ammonia, sulfide, and water supplied directly. Stepwise precursor support extends through the aminonitrile; the imine is inferred and the two hydrolysis steps remain unquantified. L-proline is a racemate component, not an isolated product.

pathways.name: Methane-ammonia-derived HCN with externally supplied acetylene
pathways.description: Adds a reducing-discharge HCN source to the reference backbone. Acetylene, sulfide, and sufficient ammonia for the aqueous branch remain cofeeds. Gas-to-water HCN recovery is an additional unquantified requirement; this is not a separately demonstrated proline-skeleton route.

pathways.name: Methane-nitrogen-derived HCN with externally supplied acetylene
pathways.description: Uses the conditional CH4/N2 discharge supply channel for HCN. Separate ammonia delivery is still required for the aza-Michael reaction. Nitrogen activation, reducing-gas availability, and HCN collection add source bottlenecks to the shared precursor and hydrolysis sequence.

pathways.name: Methane-discharge acetylene with externally supplied HCN
pathways.description: Tests discharge-generated acetylene as the C2 source while HCN is supplied independently. Productive acetylene collection from a mixed hydrocarbon gas is speculative at geological scale. The downstream proline chemistry is the same backbone as P1.

pathways.name: Carbide-derived acetylene with externally supplied HCN
pathways.description: Uses calcium carbide hydrolysis for acetylene, followed by gas delivery into the copper-containing, sulfide-poor source pool. The hydrolysis chemistry is established, but natural carbide inventory and acetylene recovery are not. The common finishing hydrolyses remain unquantified.

pathways.name: Methane-ammonia HCN supply combined with methane-discharge acetylene supply
pathways.description: Combines two discharge source channels before convergence at hydrocyanation. The first two listed reactions are parallel feedstock-generation branches, not a claim that one consumes the other's products. Simultaneous useful HCN and acetylene inventories must be measured; no paired source yield is inferred.

pathways.name: Methane-nitrogen HCN supply combined with methane-discharge acetylene supply
pathways.description: Combines the conditional CH4/N2 HCN source and methane-to-acetylene source as parallel branches feeding rxn_001. Additional ammonia and sulfide are supplied to the aqueous sequence. This variant has two unquantified source channels and does not improve evidence for the shared proline hydrolysis endpoint.

pathways.name: Methane-ammonia HCN supply combined with carbide-derived acetylene
pathways.description: Joins discharge-derived HCN and carbide-derived acetylene at the sulfide-poor copper stage. The source branches can be geographically separate because their transported products are the simple feedstocks rather than the reactive aldehyde or imine. Their capture efficiencies and delivery timing remain unmeasured.

pathways.name: Methane-nitrogen HCN supply combined with carbide-derived acetylene
pathways.description: Combines a nitrogen-activation-dependent HCN source with carbide hydrolysis. Both source modules must supply measurable feedstock flux before the common backbone is considered viable. The network does not infer natural carbide abundance or successful proline formation from a favorable bulk energy balance.

pathways.name: Direct simple feedstocks with copper-assisted C3 nitrile photoreduction
pathways.description: A process variant of P1 replacing rxn_003 with the copper-assisted alternative rxn_015. It is conditional on demonstrated catalyst survival and acceleration in the actual cyanide-sulfide mixture. It is not counted as an independently established proline-skeleton mechanism or evidence for enantioselectivity.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The backbone closely follows the supplied account of Patel et al. (2015, doi:10.1038/nchem.2202). Separating hydrocyanation from sulfidic photochemistry and trapping unstable intermediates locally are chemically sensible. The principal unresolved endpoint is successful hydrolysis under compatible surface conditions, not formation of the proline skeleton. rxn_007 remains a plausible inferred mechanistic step rather than an independently established conversion. Successful achiral hydrolysis would produce L-proline within a racemic product, without establishing enrichment or isolation.
suggestions: Supply reaction-specific pH, temperature, concentrations, irradiation dose and residence times; the referenced screening windows are not included in the submitted reaction records.
Measure aminonitrile-to-amide-to-proline conversion in representative reaction mixtures, including competing decomposition and an end-to-end yield.

Confirm proline identity and L:D composition using secondary-amine-compatible chiral analysis; investigate the transient imine and sulfur products without treating formal S8 bookkeeping as their identification.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Methane-ammonia discharge is a plausible HCN source, and rxn_011 is a valid balanced lumped channel rather than an elementary reaction. However, the submission does not establish its HCN productivity, collection efficiency or downstream-compatible product composition. Discharge amino-acid detection studies do not by themselves quantify this supply module. The shared photochemical route remains coherent, with hydrolysis to proline still unvalidated under the proposed conditions.
suggestions: Provide discharge conditions, measured HCN production and gas-to-water capture efficiency, supported by source-specific experiments.
Test whether the collected discharge mixture supports copper-mediated hydrocyanation and subsequent photochemistry without an unstated purification step.
Quantify the common hydrolysis endpoint and distinguish free proline from material released only by analytical hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: rxn_012 conserves atoms and describes a chemically possible energy-driven HCN source. Its usefulness depends on nitrogen activation, discharge product distributions and recovery of sufficient HCN, none of which is specified. The generic Surface label does not establish these operating conditions. Once suitable HCN is available, the downstream skeleton construction is the same supported route as P1, including its unresolved final hydrolysis.
suggestions: Document CH4:N2 composition, energy input, quenching and measured recoverable HCN rather than relying on the balanced source equation.
Demonstrate collection into a solution with suitable cyanide concentration and speciation for rxn_001.
Establish reaction-specific surface conditions and quantitative aminonitrile hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Methane discharge can plausibly supply acetylene, but rxn_013 is an energy-dependent net production channel, not an ordinary ambient aqueous reaction. Acetylene selectivity, cooling and delivery to the copper-mediated coupling are unspecified. These are implementation uncertainties rather than conservation failures. The downstream route remains plausible but does not establish an end-to-end proline yield.
suggestions: Measure acetylene production and survival through discharge cooling, including competing hydrocarbons and carbonaceous products.
Specify acetylene gas transfer, dissolution and retention during hydrocyanation.
Validate final hydrolysis in material produced by the complete sequence.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Calcium carbide hydrolysis is chemically well established and provides a credible acetylene source given the declared starting material. Its alkaline, exothermic source mixture nevertheless requires an explicit connection to downstream conditions. Gas transfer and direct slurry mixing have different consequences for cyanide and copper speciation. The added source step does not resolve the shared uncertainty in proline-producing hydrolysis.
suggestions: Specify whether acetylene is transferred as gas or delivered with carbide-hydrolysis liquid, and establish the resulting pH and material balance.
Document accessible carbide quantity and acetylene recovery for the proposed setting without assuming quantitative delivery.
Test the common nitrile and amide hydrolysis steps under independently justified acidic conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Both discharge source channels are chemically plausible net reactions. Their encoded stoichiometries do not establish simultaneous production, independently adjustable yields or suitable delivery ratios. If they share a discharge environment, their product distributions may be coupled; if separate, collection and mixing must be specified. The uncertainty concerns demonstrated supply and compatibility, not the number of processing steps.
suggestions: Determine whether the HCN and acetylene sources operate together or separately and measure the corresponding recoverable product distributions.
Establish feed delivery sufficient for hydrocyanation and both later HCN additions without assuming independently controllable source channels.
Carry representative source mixtures through the backbone and quantify proline formation after hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This implementation requires useful recoveries from both nitrogen-activating HCN production and methane-to-acetylene discharge chemistry. Both channels are balanceable and possible, but their joint performance and collection are unsupported by the supplied reaction records. Listing them as separate net reactions does not establish compatible source fluxes. The common hydrolysis endpoint remains an additional unresolved requirement.
suggestions: Measure HCN and acetylene yields across the actual gas composition and discharge conditions, including quench and collection losses.
Test recovered mixtures directly in rxn_001 and document any necessary separation or concentration process.
Provide a complete material balance through aminonitrile formation and subsequent proline-producing hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Carbide hydrolysis supplies acetylene through strong established chemistry, while methane-ammonia discharge provides a plausible but unquantified HCN source. Their combination is not intrinsically incompatible. However, collection, source-mixture contamination and the alkaline carbide effluent must be reconciled with hydrocyanation conditions. Neither supply option supplies new evidence for the shared final hydrolysis.
suggestions: Quantify recovered HCN from rxn_011 and acetylene delivery from rxn_014 under the stated environmental implementation.
Specify source-stream mixing or gas-transfer arrangements and verify the resulting copper and cyanide speciation.
Measure proline formation under a justified acidification and residence-time regime.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The acetylene-generating reaction is robust given calcium carbide, but the nitrogen-discharge HCN source lacks operating and recovery evidence. The connection between captured HCN, alkaline carbide-derived material and active copper hydrocyanation is also unspecified. These uncertainties affect implementation without invalidating the balanced graph or the downstream carbon-skeleton sequence.
suggestions: Provide experimentally supported HCN generation and collection data for the CH4/N2 discharge channel.
Demonstrate acetylene transfer and pH compatibility rather than assuming unrestricted mixing of source effluents.
Validate the common hydrolysis endpoint and report recoverable L-proline as a component of the total racemic product.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Copper-assisted cyanosulfidic photochemistry is consistent with the general Patel et al. literature account, so sulfide does not make rxn_015 inherently impossible. Nevertheless, activity for this substrate requires demonstrated copper speciation, ligation and resistance to precipitation under the actual formulation. Separating the earlier hydrocyanation stage does not itself establish catalyst compatibility within rxn_015. The inferred imine and unquantified final hydrolysis remain shared limitations.
suggestions: Specify copper loading, ligands, cyanide and sulfide concentrations, pH and irradiation conditions, and measure catalyst activity alongside precipitation.
Compare rxn_015 with rxn_003 under otherwise matched conditions using aldehyde-trapping yield and selectivity rather than assuming acceleration.
Link the catalyst formulation to reaction-specific experimental evidence and validate subsequent hydrolysis in its actual product mixture.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is structurally valid: its 22 molecule nodes and 15 reaction nodes form a connected graph, identifiers are used consistently, and terminal coproducts do not constitute isolated subgraphs. The supplied deterministic check establishes that all reactions conserve atoms and charge with suitable coefficients; there are no conservation violations. Coefficients of eight reflect the formal S8 representation rather than implausible elementary molecularity. H2S cancellation in rxn_007 is permissible net bookkeeping, but does not establish actual sulfur products or catalyst turnover. Literature alignment is strong for the backbone as described in the supplied Patel et al. (2015) account. The submission appropriately distinguishes the inferred imine, the reported 32% late precursor-sequence yield, unquantified hydrolysis, and feedstock alternatives from independent skeleton syntheses. Nevertheless, reaction-specific experimental citations and procedures are largely absent, and the literature summary itself notes incomplete verification of the original supplementary information. The principal network-wide gaps are the unspecified operating conditions and experimental closure of rxn_009-rxn_010. Although screening windows are mentioned, none are actually supplied in the reaction records. Surface labels alone cannot establish pH, temperature, irradiation, residence time, catalyst availability, acidification or transfer compatibility. Sulfide availability, copper speciation and source-stream recovery also require quantitative support. Successful achiral synthesis would genuinely produce L-proline as approximately half of the proline pool; no deduction is made merely for the absence of enantioenrichment or isolation. That ratio follows the achiral synthesis assumptions, not elemental balancing. Problematic-reaction flags identify unresolved mechanistic or implementation questions, not necessarily chemically impossible reactions. Overall confidence reflects the shared end-to-end limitations rather than the number of pathways, hubs or environments. The complete network is not approved at the required 0.90 threshold; individual pathway approval flags use the separately requested 0.80 threshold.
